question.prompt:
The twelve-sided figure shown has been drawn on \(1 \text{ cm}\times 1 \text{ cm}\) graph paper. What is the area of the figure in \(\text{cm}^2?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2018_AMC_8_Q04_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The slanted edges make the outline awkward to count directly. Draw the dashed segments shown below to separate a central square from four congruent triangular points.

[Figure 1](figures/2018_AMC_8_Q04_official_expansion_solution_fig1.png)

The central square \(RSTU\) is \(3\) grid units on each side, so its area is \(3\cdot3=9\). The top triangle \(REF\) has a horizontal base \(RF\) of length \(2\) and a perpendicular height of \(1\), giving area \(\frac12\cdot2\cdot1=1\). Each of the other three triangles has the same dimensions.

These five pieces fill the figure without overlap, so its area is \(9+4\cdot1=\boxed{13}\text{ cm}^2\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\). A grid outline can become easier to measure by separating a simple central region from its points.
solutions.title: Partition the outline into a square and four congruent triangles
